--- title: "Speed Factor Screenlines" subtitle: "Facility and diversion-route crossings for the SFAC sensitivity test" format: html: toc: false embed-resources: true execute: echo: false warning: false message: false jupyter: july2025 --- **[← All run sets](../../index.qmd)**  |  [Model results](results.html) *Prepared by Bill Hereth* ## Background This run set tests the effect of the network's `SFAC_BASE` speed-factor attribute — a per-link multiplier applied to free-flow speed on specific corridors — by comparing a baseline run (`sfac-base`) against a run with those factors removed (`sfac-removed`, `SpdFactor: SFAC_REMV`). To measure the effect, a dedicated set of screenlines was built covering every corridor that carries a nonzero `SFAC_BASE` value, plus a parallel/diversion-route screenline nearby for each one, so volume shifts onto alternate routes show up alongside the change on the corridor itself. These screenlines are not part of the TDM's own regional cordon set (`CVM_Screenlines_V10b.shp`, shown below in gray for context) — they're a purpose-built addition (`sfac-screenlines.shp`) layered on top of a copy of that file, applied for this run set only via the `Screenline_shp` Control Center override. ## Map Click a line for its label. Red lines are screenlines on the SFAC-affected corridors themselves; blue lines are the paired parallel/diversion facility. Long corridors (US-89, Legacy Parkway and its HOV lane, SR-193, Redwood Road, Bangerter Highway) have several screenlines spaced every 3-4 miles along their length rather than just one. ::: {#render-map .cell execution_count=4}
